issue_context.title: function "floori" returns wrong result for negative numbers
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0beta1

### System information

macOS Monterey (12.5.1), MacBook Pro, Intel Iris Plus Graphics 1536 MB

### Issue description

The function `floori` does not behave as documented for negative numbers. The documentation states that it is rounding "towards negative infinity", instead it behaves as if it is rounding "towards zero".

See the following list of examples, comparing also with the results on the float-variant, and also the other rounding functions for comparision.

Support for these functions seems to have been added here: https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/63361/commits/fdf74410150e6c8750fb251309a1f211d0db03d5

```
floori( 1.3) =  1   floor( 1.3) =  1.000000   (ok)
floori( 0.6) =  0   floor( 0.6) = -0.000000   (ok)
floori(-0.3) =  0   floor(-0.3) = -1.000000   (wrong, should be -1)
floori(-2.3) = -2   floor(-2.3) = -3.000000   (wrong, should be -3)
floori(-2.6) = -2   floor(-2.6) = -3.000000   (wrong, should be -3)
floori(-2.9) = -2   floor(-2.9) = -3.000000   (wrong, should be -3)

roundi( 1.3) =  1   round( 1.3) =  1.000000   (ok)
roundi( 0.6) =  1   round( 0.6) =  1.000000   (ok)
roundi(-0.3) =  0   round(-0.3) = -0.000000   (ok)
roundi(-2.3) = -2   round(-2.3) = -2.000000   (ok)
roundi(-2.6) = -3   round(-2.6) = -3.000000   (ok)
roundi(-2.9) = -3   round(-2.9) = -3.000000   (ok)

 ceili( 1.3) =  2    ceil( 1.3) =  2.000000   (ok)
 ceili( 0.6) =  1    ceil( 0.6) =  1.000000   (ok)
 ceili(-0.3) =  0    ceil(-0.3) = -0.000000   (ok)
 ceili(-2.3) = -2    ceil(-2.3) = -2.000000   (ok)
 ceili(-2.6) = -2    ceil(-2.6) = -2.000000   (ok)
 ceili(-2.9) = -2    ceil(-2.9) = -2.000000   (ok)
```

### Steps to reproduce

- simply use `floori` with a negative number

### Minimal reproduction project

`assert(floori(-1.6) == -2)`

review_comments:
It shouldn't return `int` in the first place as [`double` can store integers out of the `int`'s range](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Double-precision_floating-point_format#Precision_limitations_on_integer_values) (`int` isn't guaranteed to be 64-bit). It should return something like `int64_t` instead.

GDScript example (`4.0.beta1`):
```gdscript
var d = float(1 << 40)
print(d)
print(floor(d))
print(floori(d))
print(int(floor(d)))
```
Output:
```
1099511627776
1099511627776
-2147483648
1099511627776
```
All other methods are using `int` too. Should I change it all in this PR?
Yeah I guess they can all be fixed at the same time.

> All other methods are using `int` too. Should I change it all in this PR?

I know nothing, being new to contributing on Github, but if it were me, I would be inclined to create a separate PR. This PR is for fixing wrong `floori` behaviour. It makes sense to me that you should create a new PR for fixing `floori`, `ceili`, `roundi` etc. to be properly 64bit.
Fair enough, let's merge this fix first.
